takes.label: 01 / Plain
takes.description: The undecorated procedural voice, rendered from the identical 5.2-second score. No added nasal onset shaping or expressive gestures.

comments.text: Four notes begin here, but only three syllables are written. The first is la.
The pitch changes from C4 to E4 without advancing from la. This is a melisma, not another consonant.
At the intended /m/ of mi, Ear’s test measurement found a high-frequency energy share of 0.0103526. That is an acoustic measurement, not recognized wording.
At the intended /n/ of na, the measured high-frequency share was 0.0003197. The lyric still has not been independently recognized.

takes.label: 02 / Articulated
takes.description: The same notes and syllables, but Sing lengthens the nasal onsets and adjusts the transitions. Ear selected this as its acoustic development baseline.

comments.text: Listen to the initial la. Its first vowel remains the reference against which the following two consonant onsets are compared.
The pitch moves, while la continues. A single vowel carries two notes; no new syllable is triggered.
The /m/ onset’s high-frequency share falls to 0.0016679, about 84% below the plain take. This supports an onset-development decision, not intelligibility.
The /n/ onset share falls to 0.0001376, about 57% below plain. The steady vowels retain comparable spectral balance.

takes.label: 03 / Expressive
takes.description: The articulated gesture is retained while MIDI 2.0 pitch bend, breath and controlled vibrato modify the performance.

comments.text: It remains the same synthetic score: four notes, three syllables. The added movement is expression, not a new manuscript.
Try listening for the difference between a change of note and the additional, continuously varying pitch gesture.
The articulated /m/ is still present beneath pitch, breath and vibrato events. Extra musical motion need not create extra words.
Ear observed 19 spectral onset candidates in this take, versus five in each other take. They are not nineteen syllables.
